item.title: Jaxon Dart to undergo meniscus surgery on Friday
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Dart's recovery is expected to be four-to-six months.
item.content:encoded:
Jaxson Dart is going under the knife.

Per Dan Duggan of TheAthletic.com, Dart will have his knee surgery on Friday.

Dart will undergo a full meniscus repair and, if necessary, the surgeon will address his MCL and PCL. But the meniscus is Dart's primary injury.

The procedure will take place at the Hospital for Special Surgery in Manhattan.

Dart's recovery timeline is expected to be four-to-six months. That means if the Giants make it, he could possibly return for the postseason. But New York would have to make it there first.

Dart completed 26-of-34 passes for 250 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions across his two games.

item.title: The Packers' struggles could be the Jets' gain
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As the football-following world began to come to terms with the possibility that the Packers could be very bad this year, Cowboys fans began to perk up.
item.content:encoded:
As the football-following world began to come to terms with the possibility that the Packers could be very bad this year, Cowboys fans began to perk up.

Thanks to the Micah Parsons trade, the Cowboys hold Green Bay's first-round pick in 2027. So, the worse the Packers do, the higher the 2027 first-round pick climbs.

But there's an important caveat, which works to the benefit of the New York Jets.

The trade that sent defensive tackle Quinnen Williams to Dallas includes an important term as to the 2027 first-round pick the Jets received. It's not necessarily the Cowboys' pick. It's the higher of the two picks the Cowboys will have.

Which means that, if the Packers bottom out (and the Cowboys don't), the Jets get the Green Bay first-round pick in 2027.

The Jets, of course, failed to help themselves on Sunday, when they blew a 10-point lead to the Packers and mismanaged the late-game and overtime scenarios.

Still, it's good news for the Jets. Especially since they also hold the Colts' first-round pick for 2027 — and the Colts are 0-2.

item.title: Bijan Robinson and Drake London had a historic night, with 194 yards each
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Falcons running back Bijan Robinson and wide receiver Drake London ran wild at Lambeau Field on Thursday night.
item.content:encoded:
Falcons running back Bijan Robinson and wide receiver Drake London ran wild at Lambeau Field on Thursday night.

Robinson had 194 rushing yards and London had 194 receiving yards as the Falcons crushed the Packers 35-14.

Via Josh Dubow of the Associated Press, London and Robinson are the first teammates each with more than 150 yards from scrimmage in a road game at Lambeau Field. They're also the fist teammates each with 190 or more yards from scrimmage in a road game in 50 years: It was last accomplished by Rams running back Lawrence McCutcheon and wide receiver Ron Jessie at Miami in 1976.

Robinson and London have now played together in three games when they both had 150 or more yards from scrimmage. They're the first pair of teammates in NFL history to top 150 yards in the same game three times.

Robinson, who also had two catches for 19 yards, totaled 213 yards from scrimmage. He's the first player to top 200 yards from scrimmage in a game this season, and he has an NFL-high 467 yards from scrimmage this season. He's averaging 155.7 yards from scrimmage through three games.

In the first two weeks of the season, the Falcons' quarterback play was so bad with Cooper Rush getting benched for Jack Strand that it was easy to overlook what dynamic playmakers the Falcons have. If the now-healthy Michael Penix can just execute his job competently and get the ball to those playmakers consistently, the Falcons' offense is going to be a real threat for the rest of the season.

item.title: Christian Watson: We have to put a better product on the field if we want fans to have our back
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Things got ugly at Lambeau Field on Thursday night, with the Packers getting booed by the fans during their worst home loss of the Matt LaFleur era.
item.content:encoded:
Things got ugly at Lambeau Field on Thursday night, with the Packers getting booed by the fans during their worst home loss of the Matt LaFleur era.

Tucker Kraft had one response to the fans after the 35-14 loss to the Falcons.

Christian Watson had another — one that will likely play better to the fanbase.

"I mean, it’s tough. At the end of the day, it’s an entertainment business, so we’ve got to put a better product on the field if we want to have the fans have our back," Watson said, via Dominique Yates of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel. "Obviously, we’d like to think that the fans will be there through the ups and downs.

"But we’ve got to put out a better performance than that."

Watson had seven catches for 96 yards with a touchdown on Thursday night.

Now at 1-2, the Packers will be on the road in Week 4 to face the Buccaneers before home contests against the Bears and Cowboys in Weeks 5 and 6.

item.title: Brock Bowers remains limited on Thursday's injury report
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Raiders tight end Brock Bowers remained limited in Thursday's practice as he seeks to return to game action for the first time since Dec. 21.
item.content:encoded:
Raiders tight end Brock Bowers remained limited in Thursday's practice as he seeks to return to game action for the first time since Dec. 21.

Bowers is working his way back from a meniscus trim procedure earlier this month after injuring his left knee in training camp. It's the same knee that sidelined him with a PCL sprain and bone bruise during the 2025 season.

He missed five games last season.

The Raiders added defensive end Kwity Paye to the injury report with an illness. He did not practice.

Four players returned to full participation: Linebacker Nakobe Dean (shoulder), defensive tackle Folorunso Fatukasi (shoulder), cornerback Darien Porter (foot) and wide receiver Dareke Young (hamstring) were limited Wednesday.

The rest of the report was unchanged from Wednesday.

Quarterback Aidan O'Connell (personal) and safety Treydan Stukes (concussion) did not practice.

Linebacker Segun Olubi (knee) and defensive tackle JJ Pegues (back) were again full participants.

item.title: Ed Policy may regret not waiting on Matt LaFleur, Brian Gutenkunst contracts
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: After Ed Policy succeeded Mark Murphy as the president and CEO of the Packers, it quickly became clear that 2025 would be an up-or-out season for coach Matt LaFleur and G.M.
item.content:encoded:
After Ed Policy succeeded Mark Murphy as the president and CEO of the Packers, it quickly became clear that 2025 would be an up-or-out season for coach Matt LaFleur and G.M. Brian Gutekunst.

Both had contracts running through 2026. Policy made it clear that he's not a fan of lame-duck arrangements. So either they'd be extended or fired after the 2025 season.

Ultimately, the Packers made it to the playoffs as the No. 7 seed in the NFC, before blowing a 21-3 halftime lead against the Bears in the wild-card round.

That was enough, after a brief period of uncertainty, to get the Packers the give LaFleur and Gutekunst new contracts. Which, assuming that the deals guarantee one or more full seasons beyond 2026, complicates any consideration of firing either or both of them this year.

So what was the rush to extend them? There was a time when having a lame-duck coach undermined him, because the players may not respond in the desired way to a coach who may be gone after the season ends. And it's possible that Ed Policy clings to that notion in part because his father, Carmen, firmly believed in that approach when he was running the 49ers and the Browns.

Nowadays, there's a different reality in NFL locker rooms. Pro football has become a year-to-year reality, with continuity not guaranteed. The coach may be gone next year, and plenty of the players may be gone next year. All that matters is this year.

For the Packers, their coach and G.M. have a layer of job security they wouldn't have enjoyed without the extensions. It takes off some of the pressure to perform at the highest possible level, especially because firing them — and buying out their contracts — becomes a challenge for a publicly-owned team that has been, through Policy, complaining about the financial realities of a league in which the other franchises can carve off slivers of equity for many millions in new revenue.

That doesn't mean LaFleur and Gutekunst are safe. But, if they get fired, they'll get their buyouts. And the Packers will have to pay them while also paying their replacements.

In hindsight, the right move would have been to press pause on the extensions. It's a lesson both for Policy and for other owners who may end up on the fence as to the question of whether a contract should be extended in order to avoid having the coach or the G.M. work through the last year of their deals.

When in doubt, the best move may be to wait it out.

item.title: Jordan Love: Packers' run game needs to improve
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Packers quarterback Jordan Love passed for 312 yards while the running game gained 17 yards in Thursday night's loss to the Falcons, and Love says that needs to change.
item.content:encoded:
Packers quarterback Jordan Love passed for 312 yards while the running game gained 17 yards in Thursday night's loss to the Falcons, and Love says that needs to change.

The Packers' two running backs, MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson, each got only four carries. Lloyd gained 11 yards and Johnson gained six yards. Love says that's not enough.

"Our run game's got to improve. When you have a solid pass game and run game balancing each other, that always helps," Love said. "Obviously, our run game, I don't know how many rushes we had, but it's something we need to improve on right there. I think that'll help the pass game."

The Packers took a 7-0 lead in the first quarter and were tied 7-7 for most of the second quarter, but once they fell behind Love said it was harder to commit to the run.

"We got behind tonight and it didn't look good," Love said.

The Packers are hoping that their starting running back, Josh Jacobs, will play eventually this season. Jacobs is currently on paid leave and is likely to be suspended without pay after pleading no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property stemming from an incident involving his ex-girlfriend. Getting Jacobs back might help, but the Packers' running woes appear to go deeper than the running back position. Green Bay's offense needs to get better, and the Packers can't afford to wait until Jacobs returns.

item.title: Matt LaFleur on ugly loss to Falcons: "It was a butt-whooping"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The running game was MIA against ATL.
item.content:encoded:
The Packers had won 13 straight home openers. They were unable to get to 14.

The Falcons dominated at Lambeau Field on Thursday night, beating the Packers 35-14.

After the game, Green Bay coach Matt LaFleur called it what it was.

"It was a butt-whooping," LaFleur said. "That was at least three-quarter butt-whooping right there."

His comments came in the context of the potential impact of a roughing the passer call that extended Atlanta's initial scoring drive on the flow of the game. Asked about that specific call, LaFleur said, "I'm not gonna answer that. I'm not gonna get fined."

For now, no one is getting fired. Asked if the play of the offensive line will prompt changes to the coaching staff, LaFleur said, "I'm not even going to respond to that question."

He also declined to hang the sluggish performance of the offense on the blockers. "I don't want to put all the blame on the offensive line," LaFleur said. "There's enough blame to go around to everybody."

Still, the numbers say it all. The Packers couldn't run. They had nine rushing attempts for 17 yards, against 53 passes. And they clearly miss starting tailback Josh Jacobs.

"I mean, I think we all saw a dynamic running back on the other side, and I think Josh is a dynamic running back," LaFleur said. "But it is the situation, it's the circumstance. And it is what it is right now. And we've got to find a way just to either — well, one, we've got to put them in a better position, and then those guys gotta go do it."

They have extra time to figure out how to do it before a Week 4 game at Tampa Bay, for a renewal of the old NFC Central "Bay of Pigs" rivalry. With Green Bay at 1-2 and the Buccaneers at 0-2, it could be time for Chris Berman to dust off that name, for the first time in a long time.

item.title: Tucker Kraft: Disappointing that fans booed us at Lambeau Field, won't help us win
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: "It'd be much easier with the 70,000 people behind us rather than opposing us," Kraft said of the Packers fans who booed during the 35-14 loss.
item.content:encoded:
The fans in Green Bay loudly booed during the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday night at Lambeau Field. Packers tight end Tucker Kraft did not appreciate that.

"That's pretty tough," Kraft said of the booing. "Everyone pictures Lambeau Field and not boos. I don't picture boos when I picture my home stadium. That's tough. It's pretty disappointing. Especially for a home opener. It's pretty disappointing. It's not gonna help us win. I don't know what people think, that's gonna rally us or something like that. But we're grown men. We're mentally strong enough, capable enough to get back on the field and play ball. But it'd be much easier with the 70,000 people behind us rather than opposing us."

Kraft, who caught four passes for 26 yards, admitted that he didn't play to his own standards, and that the Packers need to play better than they have during their 1-2 start.

"Long season, we're three games in, we've dropped two to NFC opponents, though," Kraft said.

Kraft said the Packers can't listen to boos, cheers or anything else.

"We can't let external noise divide us," Kraft said. "Us guys in this locker room, we're really all we've got. We spend a lot of time together, so just continue to stay close and build off each other."

item.title: Thursday Night Football: Drake London, Bijan Robinson run by Packers 35-14
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: London and Robinson combined for 407 yards and two touchdowns in Michael Penix's return to the lineup.
item.content:encoded:
Drake London and Bijan Robinson combined for 407 yards and two touchdowns, leading the Falcons to a 35-14 rout of the Packers on Thursday night.

It was the Packers' first home-opening loss since 2012.

Both teams are 1-2.

After their first two games, played without starting quarterback Michael Penix, the Falcons ranked 29th in total offense (262 yards per game) and last in scoring (16 total points). They did not have a single red zone snap.

Penix's return changed everything.

He had a slow start, throwing an interception on the team's first possession, but he went 13-of-15 with a touchdown in the second and third quarters. Penix finished 18-of-25 for 256 yards with a touchdown and an interception.

London, who had six catches for 80 yards in the first two games, caught nine passes for 194 yards. Robinson, who had 37 carries for 80 yards in the first two games, had 29 carries for 194 yards and two touchdowns. He also caught two passes for 19 yards.

They are the first teammates with at least 190 yards from scrimmage in a road game since Lawrence McCutcheon and Ron Jessie did it for the Rams against the Dolphins in 1976.

The Falcons outgained the Packers 498 yards to 328, with two kneel downs in victory formation dropping them under 500 yards. They were 6-of-10 on third down.

Green Bay led 7-0 on Christian Watson's fourth touchdown catch of the season, but it was short-lived. The Falcons went on a 27-0 run before Matthew Golden scored his first touchdown.

The Packers managed only 17 yards rushing.

Jordan Love was 28-of-53 for 312 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. Golden caught five passes for 100 yards, and Watson had seven receptions for 96 yards.

item.title: Surgery not on table for Jayden Daniels, Commanders haven't discussed IR
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Daniels dislocated his left elbow in Week 2.
item.content:encoded:
Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said on Wednesday that he didn't have an update on quarterback Jayden Daniels's outlook for the coming weeks because he was still meeting with specialists about his dislocated left elbow, but General Manager Adam Peters had more to offer on Friday morning.

Daniels will not play against the Seahawks this Sunday, but Peters indicated that the Commanders expect to have the quarterback in the lineup in the near future.

“He met with doctors all over the country," Peters said, via 106.7 The Fan. "We got a lot of good opinions. As of right now, surgery is not on the table and we haven’t discussed IR.”

An injured reserve stint would keep Daniels out for at least four games, so taking that out of the conversation suggests Daniels will be ready to return to action relatively soon. For now, though, the Commanders will have to hope Marcus Mariota will be able to lead them to their first victory of the season.

item.title: Cam Skattebo: Our crowd's gotta be lit, we have a really good shot at this
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Giants learned this week that they will not have quarterback Jaxson Dart available for the rest of the 2026 season and that's dimmed their prospects for contending in the eyes of many people.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants learned this week that they will not have quarterback Jaxson Dart available for the rest of the 2026 season and that's dimmed their prospects for contending in the eyes of many people.

Running back Cam Skattebo is not part of that group. During a press conference on Thursday, Skattebo was reminded of the good vibes at MetLife Stadium from the team's Week 1 win over the Cowboys and was asked about how different things feel as they prepare to return to their home field against the Titans on Sunday.

Skattebo replied with a plea for the crowd to show up with the same energy because he doesn't believe anything has changed for the team's outlook.

"The crowd's got to be lit, just like it was the first week," Skattebo said, via a transcript from the team. "We have to have everybody's support, just like we did week one. I think the entire city of New York still knows we have a really good shot at this. And they love Jameis Winston. So, we're not going to take a step down. We're going to continue to push, continue to work. If we have our fan base with us, if they're giving everything they got towards us, I promise you they're going to get everything from us."

At 0-2, the Titans provide about as soft a landing after a tough week as the Giants could hope to find on the other side of the field. A strong performance in a win will help keep some hope alive, but a dud with Winston playing as poorly as he did in relief of Dart last Monday will make it feel real late real early for the Giants.

item.title: Kyler Murray: I've never had an issue protecting myself, concussion was an awkward play
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Kyler Murray will be back at quarterback for the Vikings when they take on the Buccaneers this Sunday and he won't be playing with fears of a repeat of what happened in Week 1.
item.content:encoded:
Kyler Murray will be back at quarterback for the Vikings when they take on the Buccaneers this Sunday and he won't be playing with fears of a repeat of what happened in Week 1.

Murray was knocked out of the Vikings' opener against the Packers after suffering a concussion while being hit by Lukas Van Ness and Javon Bullard at the end of a run. Murray said at a Thursday press conference that he felt back to himself "pretty quickly" and that the injury was a result of an unwieldy slide that put him in position to take a big shot to the head.

"I've really never had an issue protecting myself," Murray said. "I’d like to think I'm one of the least-hit quarterbacks in the league as far as just protecting myself, getting the ball out and stuff like that. That's new for me to have to go through that type of situation, because that's the last thing I ever expected is to get a concussion just because I am very careful with being in open field and I know that was kind of an awkward slide situation, but I'm always trying to protect myself. . . . Van Ness was behind me you're moving fast. You charge it to the game. I don't judge anybody over there for anything that happened. It’s part of the game."

Murray has missed plenty of other games with injuries over the course of his career, but none have come in a similar fashion as the Week 1 concussion and the Vikings will be hoping that he'll be able to avoid a repeat in the weeks to come.

item.title: Chiefs RB coach DeMarco Murray: It's hard to take Kenneth Walker out
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker is off to an impressive start to the season and the team has been giving him plenty of chances to show off his game.
item.content:encoded:
Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker is off to an impressive start to the season and the team has been giving him plenty of chances to show off his game.

Walker led the NFL in carries through the first two weeks of the season and he was tied with Jahmyr Gibbs for overall offensive touches, which led to questions for head coach Andy Reid earlier this week about whether the Chiefs should do more to manage his workload over the course of a long season. On Thursday, running backs coach DeMarco Murray fielded similar questions at a press conference.

Murray said Walker "likes the ball a lot and I like giving it to him," but acknowledged that finding ways to get rookie Emmett Johnson into the mix more often is something that is on his mind heading into the Chiefs' Week 3 game against the Dolphins.

"It’s more of a feel for me. Obviously, I want Kenneth to get into a groove and, as you guys have seen these first two games, it's hard to kind of take him out," Murray said. "But Emmett's done a great job and he's still learning. He'll continue to get more opportunities. I've just got to pull the trigger and get No. 9 out of there and put No. 10 in there."

Johnson has 103 yards on 14 touches so far this season, which makes him an appealing backup option in any week and facing an overmatched Dolphins team this weekend might make giving Walker some extra time off an even easier call for Murray and the rest of the Chiefs staff.

item.title: Drake London: Michael Penix is the definition of resiliency
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Michael Penix's return to the Falcons starting lineup didn't get off to a great start, but that just turned out to be one more chance for him to show his ability to bounce back from an adverse situation.
item.content:encoded:
Michael Penix's return to the Falcons starting lineup didn't get off to a great start, but that just turned out to be one more chance for him to show his ability to bounce back from an adverse situation.

Penix threw an interception on the fourth offensive play, which seemed like an omen that it would be a long night for the Falcons in the quarterback's first start since last season's torn ACL. It turned out far differently, however. Penix finished the night 18-of-25 for 256 yards and a touchdown to tight end Austin Hooper in a 35-14 rout of the Packers.

"I knew we had a long game ahead of us, so I just continue to keep my head down, continue to keep working and doing what I can to help this team win a football game," Penix said of his response to the interception.

Nine of Penix's passes went to wide receiver Drake London for 194 yards and the wideout had a succinct way of summing up Penix's return from both the injury and the early stumble.

"He’s the definition of resiliency," London said.

Penix noted that it is a "long season" and that the Falcons were "far from perfect" on Thursday night, but they were leaps and bounds better than they were in the first two weeks and Penix's play gives the team plenty of reason to believe that more good days are in their future.

item.title: Zach Ertz: I never wanted to leave Philadelphia, glad to be back to my favorite place
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Veteran tight end Zach Ertz has returned to Philadelphia for his second stint with the Eagles, and he says he never wanted to leave.
item.content:encoded:
Veteran tight end Zach Ertz has returned to Philadelphia for his second stint with the Eagles, and he says he never wanted to leave.

Ertz, who was drafted by the Eagles in 2013 and traded to the Cardinals in 2021, said he never knew if the Eagles would welcome him back, but always hoped they would.

"There was never a plan to come back," Ertz said. "I never wanted to leave in the first place, so let's just put that out there. The opportunity finally arose where I could come back. There's been times I asked in the past to come back and it didn't come to fruition for whatever reason. But for me, it's just a blessing to be back."

Ertz played for the Commanders last year but suffered a season-ending knee injury, and he wasn't sure if he'd be back in Philadelphia or anywhere else.

"If you told me when I got hurt that I'd be back here in nine and a half months practicing for the Philadelphia Eagles, you could have signed me up then," Ertz said. "For me, this is a place I always called home. When anyone asks my favorite place to play, everyone knows it's here"

Ertz said there are still people in the Eagles' facility who mean a lot to him, from teammates to coaches to the cafeteria staff.

"It's special," Ertz said. "It's great to see the people I've missed for a long time. It's special to be back, for sure."

Ertz said he has spent the last nine and a months rehabbing his knee with the hopes to be ready to play as soon as he signs, but that he'll let the coaching staff decide when or if he's ready to be promoted from the practice squad to the active gameday roster.

"It's up to the coaches. I'm not even on the active roster right now," Ertz said. "It's up to me to prove I can make a difference, whether it's Year 1 or Year 14."

Ertz is just glad to be back in Year 14 where it all started in Year 1.

item.title: Ruling on key sealed document in Brian Flores case is also under seal, for now
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Brian Flores case against the NFL and several teams (Dolphins, Texans, Giants, and Broncos) has recently focused on a document produced by Korn Ferry, in connection with a coaching search the company performed for the Ravens.
item.content:encoded:
The Brian Flores case against the NFL and several teams (Dolphins, Texans, Giants, and Broncos) has recently focused on a document produced by Korn Ferry, in connection with a coaching search the company performed for the Ravens.

Korn Ferry and the NFL want the document to remain under seal and, as a result, not available to the public. Flores has challenged the designation.

In most federal civil cases, the presiding judge delegates disputes that arise during the discovery process to a magistrate judge. In this case, the magistrate judge has issued a ruling.

The ruling, as reported by Daniel Kaplan, is also under seal. For now.

The apparent reason for the decision is to give the party that lost the issue a chance to appeal to the presiding judge. And the fact that the decision is sealed doesn't necessarily mean Korn Ferry lost. In order to issue the preliminary ruling, the magistrate judge likely had to quote from or otherwise describe key aspects of the currently secret document.

If the case goes to trial, the document undoubtedly will be presented and discussed in open court. But that's a long way away. Securing the publication of the document sooner rather than later could create a bad P.R. look for the league, which could not only spark meaningful settlement talks but also prompt the media, the fans, and those with oversight of the league to sit up and take notice of the manner in which the sausage gets made.

For now, the question is whether the losing party on the issue of the sealed document will appeal within the 14-day time period for doing so. And whoever files the appeal necessarily will have been the losing party.

item.title: Thursday Night Football: Falcons lead Packers 17-7 at halftime
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Michael Penix is back . . . and so are the Falcons.
item.content:encoded:
Michael Penix is back . . . and so are the Falcons.

The quarterback, who hadn't played since Nov. 16, got off to a slow start. His third pass was an interception and he was only 5-of-11 to start. Penix, though, found his groove, finishing the first half 13-of-20 for 114 yards with a touchdown and an interception.

His 5-yard touchdown throw to tight end Austin Hooper on third-and-goal with 59 seconds left in the half has the Falcons in the locker room with a 17-7 lead at halftime.

The Falcons, who did not have a red zone snap in the first two games, are 2-for-2 in the red zone tonight. They scored on three of their last four possessions in the first half.

Falcons running back Bijan Robinson has 15 carries for 111 yards, including a 3-yard touchdown run. He also has one catch for 17 yards.

Drake London has five catches for 54 yards.

The Falcons have outgained the Packers 253 to 108. Green Bay went three-and-out on four of six possessions in the first half, going 1-for-6 on third down with four punts.

Green Bay kicker Trey Smack had his 47-yard field goal try blocked by Falcons defensive lineman Zach Harrison.

Jordan Love is 9-of-19 for 96 yards, including a 4-yard touchdown pass to Christian Watson. It is Watson's fourth touchdown of the season. Matthew Golden has two catches for 53 yards.

The Green Bay run game is nonexistent with five carries for 12 yards from MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson.

The Packers have won 13 consecutive home openers at Lambeau Field.

item.title: On Thursday, Mike McCarthy didn't want to say much about Joey Porter Jr.'s status
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On Wednesday, Steelers coach Mike McCarthy wasn't asked about cornerback Joey Porter Jr.
item.content:encoded:
On Wednesday, Steelers coach Mike McCarthy wasn’t asked about cornerback Joey Porter Jr. On Thursday, McCarthy was.

He didn't seem to like it very much.

After McCarthy said Porter, who was officially limited in practice on Wednesday, is scheduled “to do some more today, so we’ll see how that goes,” McCarthy was asked whose decision it was for Porter to be limited on Wednesday.

“We have a plan for every one of our players," McCarthy said, via Brandon Contes of Awful Announcing. "So, he did the work that was planned on."

McCarthy then was asked whether that means it was the team's plan for Porter to be limited.

“We’re not gonna play this game anymore about every little question,” McCarthy said. "You can just see [P.R. director] Burt [Lauten] for the injury report."

And here's where a strange situation becomes even more strange. On Wednesday, the team's website listed Porter as limited with this designation: "not injury related — conditioning." The NFL's official report, which is distributed via email, said on both Wednesday and Thursday that Porter was limited due to "not injury related — other."

The team's website, as of this posting, contains no specific injury description for any of the injured Steelers players: Porter, Jamel Dean, Rico Dowdle, Gennings Dunker, Cole Holcomb, Michael Pittman Jr., Jalen Ramsey, or Jaylen Warren.

While it's possible that the error is clerical (frankly, we can't recall ever seeing a team website omitting the specific source of the injury for its players), the deeper issue here is whether the Steelers' representations to the world regarding Porter's status will become relevant if/when the Steelers decide to play hardball with Porter.

If they've been officially saying Porter is injured (for Week 1, it was "back" and for Week 2, it was "back" and "conditioning"), it becomes awkward for the Steelers to suddenly contend that he was fine all along, if they ever choose to do that.

Either way, the tension seems to be increasing. As evidenced by McCarthy's reaction to fair and reasonable questions about Porter that were posed to the head coach on Thursday.

item.title: Joe Flacco: I have no reason to believe I'm getting traded
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: "I had no idea I was going to get traded last year, so you never know," Flacco added of a potential trade to the Giants.
item.content:encoded:
Bengals quarterback Joe Flacco is not on the trade block. That he knows of.

Flacco said today that after Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart got hurt, friends of his thought he was going to get traded to the Giants and reunited with coach John Harbaugh. Flacco had to tell them it wasn't happening.

"It's obviously not real and not true, but it was good enough to get people, certain friends of mine, to text me, 'Hey I'll see you in New York.' I was like, 'No, guys, you won’t, that's not true,'" Flacco told Kelsey Conway of the Cincinnati Enquirer.

Flacco said he's committed to the Bengals unless and until they tell him they're trading him.

"It's not up to me. I'm on the Cincinnati Bengals, and because of that, that's my focus, is just being here, and doing the things I need to do to get better each day while I'm here," Flacco said. "I get a little bit of a kick out of it, but it's kind of out of my hands. . . . I'm a Cincinnati Bengal and I'm doing everything I can to get ready for the Pittsburgh Steelers."

Last year the Browns traded Flacco to the Bengals after Joe Burrow was injured, and Flacco acknowledged that he wouldn't necessarily know if a trade was coming.

"I had no idea I was going to get traded last year, so you never know," Flacco said. "But no, I have no reason to believe that. No."

item.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown says he was fined nearly $60,000 for four smoking-related celebrations
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The No Fun League has cracked down particularly hard on celebrations this week.
item.content:encoded:
Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown told reporters today that he was fined nearly $60,000 for four celebrations in which he mimicked smoking in last week's game against the Bills.

St. Brown said each of his four celebrations came with a fine of more than $14,000.

“It’s not good, man," St. Brown said, via the Detroit Free Press. "Fourteen-something times four. You do the math. But I’m appealing."

The NFL classifies inappropriate celebrations as unsportsmanlike conduct, and the standard fine is $14,926. Four of those fines would total $59,704.

The league appears to have cracked down especially hard on celebrations this week. 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk was fined for what the league said was miming chugging a beer but Juszczyk says was miming drinking a glass of juice, which is his nickname. Colts guard Matt Goncalves was fined for the same thing. Bengals receivers Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins were both fined for a celebration that was deemed to be obscene.

item.title: Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins fined for celebrations the league deemed obscene
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The NFL is sometimes called the No Fun League.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL is sometimes called the No Fun League. Apparently, it's also the No Phallus League.

Yes, I've now seen everything. (Not literally.)

The league fined Bengals receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins for a celebration that was deemed to be obscene.

From Jonathan Jones of The Athletic: "On multiple occasions last week, Chase and Higgins each did a gesture that can be interpreted as resembling a phallus."

In a session with reporters, Chase explained that the gesture is a variation of "the people's elbow," a move made popular by Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

"Bro, at the end of the day, I can't say what something we made up, and then everybody else saying what it is," Chase said, via Pat Brennan of the Cincinnati Enquirer. "I can't sit there and say that.

"Everybody gonna have their opinion on what it look like, what it is. They had many people talking about what it looked like, what it is but I can't really sit here and say, 'That's what it is.' You know? Obviously, that's not what it is, but it is what it is."

Some people other than the powers-that-be at 345 Park Avenue did indeed interpret the celebration as referring to the display of a body part other than an elbow.

Chase displayed a potentially acceptable alternative during his Wednesday press conference.

The disclosure comes on the same day that news emerged of a fine imposed on 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk for, in the league's view, miming the chugging of a beer.

Chase suggested that the league's "superstars" should work with the NFL Players Association and "fight for our money."

While it makes no sense to fine Juszczyk for pretending to do what thousands of fans literally do while attending NFL games, the Chase and Higgins fines become the logical extension of the punishment, since that's where the chugged beer quickly ends up.
